youtube.title: Why You Can't Hum With Your Nose Closed 🤐 #Shorts
youtube.description:
Pinch your nose, close your mouth, and try to hum. It stops.

When you hum, your voice needs air flowing out of you. With your mouth closed, that air has only one way out. Your nose. Block the nose too, and the air has nowhere to go. Pressure builds in your mouth and throat for a second or two. Then your vocal cords can't vibrate any more, and the hum dies. So every hum you've ever made was really your nose singing.

Watch our full episodes on the channel.
